newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 97 GDP growth seen at 5.7 pct despite flood.
newsitem.headline: Polish 97 GDP growth seen at 5.7 pct despite flood.

text.p: Poland's gross domestic product should grow 5.7 percent this year against 6.1 percent in 1996 as the negative effects of July's floods in the south of the country will be limited, a senior government analyst said.

Zbigniew Kuzmiuk, head of the state Centre for Strategic Studies (CSS) told a news conference on Wednesday the growth would be mainly fuelled by industrial production growth, construction and investment.
"The flood and its effects have to some extent disrupted economic processes but according to current estimates they will not break the fast growth of the economy," Kuzmiuk said.
He said the strong, seven percent GDP rise in the first half of the year guaranteed that even if a slow-down in the second half occurred, overall annual growth would stay high.
Kuzmiuk noted the good business climate in the first half of the year was based on domestic demand, both investment and consumption.
He said the floods, which inudated a total of 6,000 sq km killing 54 people and causing damage running into billions of dollars, would not have much effect on industrial production this year.
"We predict that in 1997, as in 1996, total industral production will grow 8.5 percent, and in companies employing more than five persons -- nine percent," Kuzmiuk said.
"The effect of the flood on production and financial standing of the whole industry is likely to be small," he said.
He said reconstruction work in areas affected by the floods was even expected to boost the output of the construction sector, fuelling GDP growth.
"We estimate that the production of medium and large construction firms may be up to 25 percent higher than in 1996 and toghether with small firms up to 20 percent," Kuzmiuk said.
Kuzmiuk said investment growth this year was likely to remain very high at 20 percent against 1996, higher than the previously estimated 18 percent.

"The higher than expected investment is related to reconstruction work on buildings and infrastructure destroyed by the flood for which there will be special funds from the state budget and local budgets as well as domestic and foreign credit lines and aid," he said.
